rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes helium-ion irradiation, whereas the paper studied an as-cast WTaTiVZr refractory high-entropy alloy compared with pure tungsten; these are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies 500–1000 °C helium irradiation, while the paper used room-temperature compression, indentation from 25–500 °C, and room-temperature scratch testing; the conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility, whereas the paper attributes behavior to solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and dislocation-core modification from alloying elements; these are contradictory mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased plastic strain and toughness from irradiation, while the paper predicts and measures higher strength, plasticity, and toughness from alloying with Ti, V, Zr, and Ta; the property direction is similar but the cause and context are completely different.
